Configuration.AuthFlowNote: Vanilla API v2 documents two means of server-to-server authentication that both resolve to the SAME Bearer-token shape (KB article 41, 'Authenticating API v2 calls with Personal Access Tokens'): (1) a Personal Access Token generated per-user from the user's own profile (MeBox > Edit Profile > Access Tokens > Generate New Token), gated by the 'Garden > Tokens > Add' permission on the generating user's Role -- this is the connector's PRIMARY/chosen auth path, classified api-key because it is a static, manually-issued, long-lived token with no OAuth handshake; (2) a JWT addon (KB article 122, 'Authenticating API v2 calls with JWT') that lets a server sign its own short-lived HS256 JWT (claims: iss/sub/aud/email/displayname/exp/iat-or-nbf) and pass it as a Bearer token -- a genuine documented ALTERNATIVE to a PAT, requires the JWT addon + a shared secret configured in Vanilla's JWT settings, recorded here as awareness (not the connector's chosen path). API calls made with a Personal Access Token reflect the permissions of the user who generated it (no separate service-account concept).
Configuration.AuthHeaderPatternNote: KB article 41 (verbatim): 'To authenticate with the HTTP header, pass the access token in the Authorization field with the bearer scheme.' A query-string fallback (?access_token=<token>) is also documented for clients that cannot set custom headers or want to avoid CORS preflight, but the header form is vendor-recommended ('headers are not usually logged on servers') and is what this connector uses.

jwtApiAuth.timestampClaim: iat or nbf (at least one required; a token with neither, or one set in the future, is rejected)
jwtApiAuth.note: Confirmed via a live credential-free fetch of KB article 122 (https://success.vanillaforums.com/kb/articles/122-authenticating-api-v2-calls-with-jwt). A documented ALTERNATIVE to the Personal Access Token, not the connector's chosen path -- recorded here as awareness per the build's explicit instruction. Requires the JWT addon + a shared HMAC secret configured server-side in Vanilla's Dashboard JWT settings (kept secret; a leaked secret should be rotated immediately per the vendor's own warning). Distinct from the JWT-based end-user SSO web flow the same addon also enables (see EndUserSSOMechanisms below) -- this API-auth usage is explicitly for machine/server-to-server API calls, independent of the web sign-in flow.

roleTokens.lifetimeMinutes: 1 to 3 (a 2-minute expiration window with a 1-minute rollover)
roleTokens.identityScope: Roles/permissions ONLY -- carries no userID or sessionID claim, so it CANNOT be used anywhere a user identity is required
roleTokens.purpose: An HTTP-cache-friendly authorization mechanism (lets Vanilla's CDN/browser cache share one cached response across many authorized users who share the same Roles) -- NOT a general-purpose API credential.
roleTokens.note: Confirmed via a live credential-free fetch of KB article 436 (https://success.vanillaforums.com/kb/articles/436-authenticating-api-v2-calls-with-role-tokens). Named explicitly per the build's instruction even though it is NOT and cannot be the connector's primary auth mechanism -- it is limited to exactly 3 read-only endpoints and carries no user identity, so it cannot drive a general sync. Recorded as vendor-domain awareness only.

flavors: JWT-based SSO (the same JWT addon also drives a web sign-in flow, distinct from its API-auth usage above)
EndUserSSOMechanisms.role: END-USER community sign-in / identity-federation flows configured in the Vanilla Dashboard (Settings > Authentication) -- these authenticate a HUMAN into the forum UI. They are NOT the connector's server-to-server API auth path and this connector does not use them.
EndUserSSOMechanisms.evidence: Named explicitly in the operator's Tier-3 context document (packages/Integration/connectors-registry/higherlogic-vanilla/sources/contextHLV.md) as real Vanilla product concepts; recorded here for connector-author awareness/disambiguation only -- no Tier-1/2 hard-constraint claim is made about their configuration surface, and none is needed since they play no role in this connector's auth flow.

Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: UNDOCUMENTED / not applicable in the conventional OAuth2 refresh_token sense. KB article 41 describes Personal Access Tokens as manually generated from the user's profile with no stated expiry, TTL, or refresh endpoint/grant -- they appear to be long-lived until manually revoked by the user (Access Tokens page) or their generating Role's 'Garden > Tokens > Add' permission is revoked. Left null rather than fabricated per the InferredFromContext-rejected-for-hard-constraints rule; the connector should treat a 401 as the signal to alert for re-issuance of a new Personal Access Token, not assume a refresh_token grant exists.

PerTenantConfig.note: Vanilla is a per-tenant hosted (or self-hosted) community product -- there is no single global API host. Every credential-free source in this build's evidence trail confirms the pattern via its OWN community's servers entry (open.vanillaforums.com/api/v2 and success.vanillaforums.com/api/v2 -- two DIFFERENT communities' OpenAPI documents both declare `servers: [{url: '<own-host>/api/v2'}]`, i.e. the API version path segment 'api/v2' is constant but the host is per-community). Per the tenant-agnostic metadata rule, NO literal tenant community URL is baked into this file -- GetBaseURL must template `{communityUrl}/api/v2` from the CompanyIntegration's own Configuration/credential value at runtime. `communityUrl` is the proposed non-secret config key name identity-establisher's CredentialTypeID match-or-create should use (paired with the secret Personal Access Token) -- e.g. the existing `metadata/credential-types/schemas/api-key-with-endpoint.schema.json` shape ({apiKey (secret), endpoint (non-secret, uri)}) is a structural match if identity-establisher chooses to reuse/adapt it, though the exact CredentialTypeID decision belongs to that stage, not this one.

PaginationDefaults.navigationMechanism: Link response header (RFC 5988 style) -- NOT a body-embedded cursor. rel values: first, last, prev (only if page>1), next (only if more records available).
PaginationDefaults.pagingContinuesHeaderNote: Per KB article 40: results-per-page can be LOWER than `limit` even when more pages remain (rows can be stripped by the requesting user's permissions after the DB query ran, which can also produce empty-but-not-final pages) -- the `Paging-Next` response header is the reliable 'more data exists' signal, NOT merely `results.length === limit`.
PaginationDefaults.alternatePaginationStyle: 'more' pagination (first/prev/next relations only, no `last`) -- used on resources where computing a total row COUNT would be expensive; still delivered via the same Link header mechanism.
PaginationDefaults.advanceProtocol: 1. Issue the request with page=1&limit=<N> (and any fields=... sparse fieldset). 2. Parse the Link response header for rel="next" (RFC 5988: `<url>; rel="next"`). 3. If present (or if the Paging-Next header is present), follow that exact URL for the next page (it already carries the correct page/limit query params) -- do not hand-increment `page` if a next-page Link/header is absent even when a full-size page was returned, since a filtered/permission-trimmed page can look 'full' without there being more data, and conversely a short page can still have more.
PaginationDefaults.note: Confirmed via the merged OpenAPI v3 spec's own query-parameter declarations (335-path union of open.vanillaforums.com + success.vanillaforums.com; see extract-integration-config-facts.mjs paginationSample output) plus KB article 40 ('API v2 Overview') prose. An 'X-App-Page-*' response-header family was named in this build's own planning brief but could NOT be confirmed in ANY credential-free source consulted (not the merged OpenAPI spec's declared response headers, not KB article 40's raw HTML, not the operator's context doc) -- it is explicitly NOT asserted here; treat it as an unconfirmed claim pending live-probe verification, not a fact.

IncrementalSyncCapability.mechanism: A `dateUpdated` (or, on insert-only/no-update resources, `dateInserted`) query parameter documented on list endpoints as 'Filter by update/insert date' (OpenAPI parameter description, linking to a vendor date-filters guide for the exact operator syntax).
IncrementalSyncCapability.scope: Confirmed present (via the merged OpenAPI spec's own parameter declarations) on the /discussions, /users, and /comments list endpoints spot-checked directly; the door-level catalog (sources/derived/enumerate-vanilla-catalog.output.json) shows 23 of the 51 coverable objects carry a `dateUpdated` field/watermark and a further 10 are insert-only (`dateInserted` only, no update timestamp) -- per-object IncrementalWatermarkField assignment is the extractor's job, using this same OpenAPI evidence per-object rather than a single vendor-wide constant, since NOT every coverable object documents the filter (e.g. /categories and /roles do not expose a dateUpdated filter param in the spot-check).
IncrementalSyncCapability.dateFilterDocReference: https://docs.vanillaforums.com/help/apiv2/date-filters/ (referenced inline by the OpenAPI parameter descriptions; this URL renders the same Success-Community KB SPA shell as success.vanillaforums.com per SOURCES.json, so it is not treated as an independent corpus, only as the vendor's own pointer to the date-filter operator syntax).

Configuration.WebhooksNote: Confirmed via a live credential-free fetch of KB article 262 ('Webhooks', https://success.vanillaforums.com/kb/articles/262-webhooks) plus the merged OpenAPI spec's Webhook/WebhookPost/WebhookPatch schemas (full CRUD: GET/POST /webhooks, GET/PATCH/DELETE /webhooks/{id}, plus GET /webhooks/{id}/deliveries for delivery history). Verbatim from the KB article: 'Every webhook delivery sent by Vanilla includes a X-Vanilla-Signature header... Vanilla currently uses the SHA-1 algorithm to generate a hash-based message authentication code (HMAC) using the webhook's configured Secret.' The Webhook schema's own `secret` field description corroborates: 'The secret used to sign events associated with this webhook.' The Webhooks addon is per-tenant and 'must be enabled by Vanilla staff' (KB article 262) -- i.e. NOT guaranteed present on every customer community; runtime discovery (a 404/403 on /webhooks) is the correct per-tenant signal, not a build-time assumption of universal availability. Documented event families (KB article 262): Article, Answer, Comment, Community Event, Discussion, Escalation, Group, Notification, Reaction, Report, User, Warnings & Notes.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: No general bulk create/update/delete endpoint (a single request carrying multiple heterogeneous records) is documented anywhere in the 335-path merged OpenAPI union. Two narrow, single-purpose bulk ACTION endpoints exist (POST /discussions/resolve-bulk to mark multiple discussions resolved; POST /badges/{id}/bulk-users to award one badge to multiple users) -- neither is a general-purpose batch-write mechanism for arbitrary objects, so BulkOperationsAvailable is honestly false at the vendor-wide level. Separately, an async /exports resource (full CRUD: GET/POST /exports, GET/DELETE /exports/{exportUUID}, GET /exports/{exportUUID}/download) supports bulk DATA EXPORT (not write) as CSV, and the `fields` sparse-fieldset query param is documented to also work with CSV export (KB article 40).
Configuration.APIVersioningNote: Both credential-free source communities' OpenAPI documents declare `servers: [{"url": "<own-host>/api/v2"}]` -- the API major version ('v2') is embedded as a literal path segment on every one of the 335 documented operation paths, with no separate version header or query parameter observed anywhere in the merged spec.

ErrorResponseShape.note: The merged OpenAPI spec's `BasicError` component schema ({message: string (required), status: integer (required)}) is referenced by 4xx/5xx responses across the union spec (15 explicit references found in a direct scan of every operation's 4xx/5xx response content -- see extract-integration-config-facts.mjs errorSchema output) -- by far the dominant error shape (compare a single, addon-scoped `Error` schema variant {message, code} used only by the Salesforce third-party-integration config endpoints, which is NOT the general API error shape).

Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPatternNote: No vendor-documented naming convention for a dynamically-named CUSTOM OBJECT family was found anywhere in the 380-schema merged spec (no HubSpot-style p_<accountID>_<name> pattern, no generic 'custom object' resource door). Vanilla's API v2 extensibility surface is fixed/first-class objects (Categories, Discussions, Groups, Subcommunities, Products, Knowledge Bases, etc.) plus admin-configurable Profile Fields (see CustomFieldMarkerPattern) -- there is no mechanism by which a tenant creates an entirely new, independently-addressable custom OBJECT type via API v2.
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPatternNote: Vanilla's customer-extensibility surface for FIELDS is the admin-configurable Profile Field (`GET/POST /profile-fields`, `apiName` string business-key PK). The OpenAPI schema describes `apiName` only as 'The ID of the profile field' with no documented prefix/suffix naming convention (e.g. no p_<x>_ style marker) -- it is a free-form identifier chosen by the community admin when the field is created (Settings > Membership > User Profile > Custom Profile Fields, per KB article 262's cross-reference). Profile Fields are themselves a first-class, fully runtime-discoverable IO (`/profile-fields`) rather than a naming-convention-marked subset of an existing object's fields, so no CustomFieldMarkerPattern regex/prefix is needed for discovery -- the extractor/runtime discovery surfaces them as their own object.

WriteCapability.scope: Substantial and vendor-wide, NOT a narrow exception. Of the 51 coverable objects enumerated from the merged OpenAPI spec (sources/derived/enumerate-vanilla-catalog.output.json, cross-checked via extract-integration-config-facts.mjs writeStats): 37 support Create, 33 support Update, 32 support Delete, and 25 support full Create+Update+Delete. Only 8 of 51 are read-only end-to-end (AutomationDispatch, ProductMessage, RoleApplication, Sessions, OnlineUser/UserFragment, UserMention, UserNote, Widget) -- all of these are either system-generated logs/history (AutomationDispatch run history, Sessions), presence/mention feeds (OnlineUser, UserMention), or admin-curated read surfaces with no documented write endpoint (UserNote, Widget, ProductMessage).

notablePartialWriteObjects.Article: Create (POST /articles) + Update (PATCH /articles/{id}) but NO DELETE endpoint -- deletion is a soft, status-based transition via PATCH /articles/{id}/status (see DeleteSemantics).
notablePartialWriteObjects.Conversation/Message: Create + list only, no update/delete documented.

WriteCapability.sourceUrl: sources/vanilla-openapi.merged.v3.json (union of https://open.vanillaforums.com/api/v2/openapi/v3 and the success.vanillaforums.com KB-1842-embedded spec)
WriteCapability.note: This is BINDING evidence against a pull-only connector for this vendor -- Vanilla is genuinely, substantially write-capable across the majority of its coverable object surface, not merely a read API with a couple of incidental write endpoints.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No `If-Match`, `ETag` response header, `If-Unmodified-Since`, or a record-level revision/version field for optimistic-concurrency purposes was found anywhere in the 380-schema merged OpenAPI spec (a direct case-insensitive scan for these tokens across the full spec text found exactly 4 'etag'-adjacent hits, ALL of which are unrelated false positives on inspection: an unrelated file-upload-part `eTag` field on a multipart-upload schema, two accidental substring matches inside the unrelated schema name `DeleteTagInfo`, and a client-side `CacheBusterParameter` query parameter literally named `etag` used for cache-busting -- NOT an HTTP conditional-write/optimistic-concurrency mechanism. See extract-integration-config-facts.mjs concurrencyControlSignals.etagContexts for the exact matched substrings.). Objects do carry `dateUpdated`/`articleRevisionID`-style informational timestamps/revision IDs (the latter only on Article, for its revision-history feature -- not a general optimistic-lock token), but none is documented as a conditional-write precondition. Any future bidirectional EntityMap must use snapshot-3-way conflict resolution only -- do not recommend MostRecent.
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsDetail: Vendor-wide: HARD delete is the default and dominant pattern -- a real HTTP DELETE verb is documented on 32 of 51 coverable objects (spot-checked directly: DELETE /discussions/{id}, /comments/{id}, /users/{id}, /categories/{id}, /groups/{id}, /roles/{id}, /badges/{id}, /webhooks/{id}, etc.), and none of these objects' schemas document an accompanying soft-delete/archive/tombstone field (no `isDeleted`/`archived`/`status=deleted` property found on Discussion, Comment, User, Category, or Group). ONE documented, NAMED EXCEPTION: Article has NO DELETE endpoint at all (confirmed absent from /articles/{id}'s operation list, which is GET+PATCH only) -- article deletion/restoration is instead a SOFT, status-based transition via `PATCH /articles/{id}/status` with an explicit enum `{"undeleted", "deleted", "published"}` on the Article schema's own `status` property. This exactly matches the Webhooks KB article's own webhook-event description ('A webhook event fires when an article is Added / Edited / Deleted / Restored... when an article is deleted or restored, it fires as an article_update event') -- i.e. Vanilla's own documentation independently confirms Articles are restorable (soft-deleted), while a real DELETE-verb object like Discussion or Comment has no such restore path documented anywhere in this evidence trail.
Configuration.DefaultSyncDirectionNote: Read-only default for every object per the read-first, bidirectional-opt-in safety discipline, regardless of the substantial documented write surface (37/51 objects support Create). Bidirectional sync requires sandbox validation against a real or test Vanilla community first -- see BidirectionalPreconditions below.
Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReason: ConcurrencyControl=none (no ETag/If-Match/version field documented anywhere in the 380-schema merged spec, and the 4 'etag'-adjacent spec hits are confirmed false positives -- see ConcurrencyControlNote) rules out MostRecent as a safe default, since MostRecent requires a reliable revision/timestamp-of-write signal to arbitrate conflicts that Vanilla does not expose at the API level. DestWins is the conservative default if/when any of the 37 create-capable / 33 update-capable objects is later enabled for bidirectional sync -- it overwrites the MJ destination with Vanilla's source-of-truth on pull, avoiding silent conflict-loss in either direction until a real concurrency signal is discovered (e.g. via a future live-probe finding an undocumented revision field).
BidirectionalPreconditions: Obtain a live/sandbox Vanilla community + a real Personal Access Token and empirically confirm the actual request/response shape of each write path this build only knows from the merged OpenAPI spec's documented schemas -- never yet exercised against a live server in this credential-free run.

Confirm the true delete behavior per object empirically: this evidence trail shows HARD delete (no soft-delete field) on 31 of 32 delete-capable objects and a documented SOFT/status-based delete on Article only -- a live probe should confirm no other object has an undocumented soft-delete/trash mechanism before treating any DELETE as safe to run against a client's real community content.

Confirm whether any object exposes an undocumented concurrency/versioning signal at the live API layer (current evidence: none) before ever recommending MostRecent conflict resolution over the current DestWins default.

Confirm the true lifetime/revocation behavior of a Personal Access Token in practice (currently UNDOCUMENTED beyond 'generated from the user profile, no stated expiry') so credential rotation and long-running-sync retry semantics can be implemented correctly.

Validate write behavior (especially DELETE on Discussion/Comment/User/Category/Group and the soft-delete PATCH /articles/{id}/status transition) against a sandbox/test Vanilla community before any bidirectional EntityMap touches a client's real community/member data -- per the read-first, bidirectional-opt-in discipline, this must never be turned on by default.

Confirm per-tenant addon availability (Knowledge Base, Webhooks, AI settings, third-party integration configs are all addon-gated and vary per customer community) via runtime discovery before assuming a given write-capable object is actually present/enabled on a specific customer's community.

RateLimitPolicy.hardLimitConsequence: The IP may become blocked, requiring MANUAL intervention by Vanilla Support to remove the block (not an automatic lift like the standard 429 case).
RateLimitPolicy.note: Verbatim from KB article 44 ('Rate Limits'): 'GET requests... are limited to 300 requests per 1 minute, per IP.' / 'POST / PUT / PATCH / DELETE requests... are limited to 120 requests per 1 minute, per IP.' / 'Exceeding the following rate limits will result in a temporary block, during which the service will respond with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. The block will lift automatically after 1 minute.' / 'If you send more than 250 requests within 10 seconds, your IP may become blocked and require manual intervention by Vanilla Support in order to remove the block.' No `Retry-After` header, `X-RateLimit-*` header family, or any other rate-limit-signaling response header is documented in this KB article OR declared anywhere in the 380-schema merged OpenAPI spec's response headers (confirmed by a direct scan -- see extract-integration-config-facts.mjs; the only x-prefixed response headers found anywhere are `x-file-rehosted-failed-count`/`x-file-rehosted-success-count`, unrelated to rate limiting) -- recorded honestly as retryAfterHeaderDocumented=false rather than assumed. Root Integration.BatchMaxRequestCount/BatchRequestWaitTime are set to the broader/primary GET limit (300 requests / 60 seconds) per the sibling-connector convention of promoting the LESS restrictive vendor-wide limit to the root fields; the MORE restrictive write limit (120/60) and the 250-per-10-second hard block threshold are recorded here in full for the connector's RateLimitPolicy override to consume.

Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeRationale: Set to FALSE (the conservative/safe default) despite one CANDIDATE endpoint worth flagging for a future iteration: every Vanilla community serves its own live OpenAPI v3 document at `{communityUrl}/api/v2/openapi/v3` (this build's own two source specs were fetched from exactly this endpoint on two different communities -- see SOURCES.json), and it IS permission-gated on at least one tested community (success.vanillaforums.com returns HTTP 403 'Garden.Settings.Manage' for anonymous requests; open.vanillaforums.com serves it unauthenticated). The two communities' specs also differ in size (237 vs. 316 paths) in a way CONSISTENT with per-community addon-scoping. However, this build could NOT confirm (credential-free) whether that size difference reflects (a) a genuinely per-tenant, permission-scoped, complete-gamut catalog of what THIS credential can access, or (b) merely a different installed product/addon build being served identically to every caller regardless of the caller's own permissions -- both are consistent with the observed evidence, and connector-code-conventions.md requires EVIDENCE the endpoint 'enumerates the COMPLETE gamut the credentials expose' before flipping this flag, not a plausible hypothesis. No CODE PATH in this connector build (Declared-metadata-only, no live DiscoverObjects/DiscoverFields implementation yet) calls this endpoint, so there is also no implementation evidence to point to. Recorded here as a CANDIDATE for CodeBuild/a future iteration to empirically resolve via a live-credentialed probe (does the SAME community's /openapi/v3 response change when queried with tokens from users holding different permission sets, and does it omit an addon-disabled door only in the way the addon actually differs?) -- until then, DiscoveryIsAuthoritative stays FALSE per the safe default: per-tenant addon variance (Knowledge Base, Webhooks, AI settings, third-party integration configs, custom Profile Fields) means any given customer community exposes a DIFFERENT subset of the 51 coverable objects than another (e.g. a community without the Knowledge Base addon will 404 on /knowledge-bases), and the BaseRESTIntegrationConnector default (cache-driven IntrospectSchema re-reading persisted ACTIVE metadata, itself non-authoritative) applies. Runtime DiscoverObjects/DiscoverFields for this connector, if implemented against a live community, would today be SCOPED to that tenant's actually-enabled addons -- so absence of an object on a comprehensive refresh must NOT deactivate it (it may simply be an addon this tenant hasn't enabled, or the tenant's token lacks the permission to see it), per connector-code-conventions.md's authoritative-discovery + deactivation rule. Custom (admin-configured) Profile Fields ARE fully runtime-discoverable via the `/profile-fields` door and flow through ordinary Discovered-metadata + the framework's custom-column capture, independent of this authoritative-discovery decision.
Configuration.OutOfScopeObjectFamiliesRationale: No out-of-scope product family was identified by SourceAudit (SOURCE_STUDY.md §8 scopeDecision: 'none identified'). Both credential-free source communities probed (open.vanillaforums.com and success.vanillaforums.com) are live instances of the SAME single, unified Vanilla API v2 contract -- they simply have different ADDON subsets enabled (Knowledge Base/Articles/Analytics/AI-settings on success.vanillaforums.com only; a broader core forum/discussion feature set with no Knowledge Base on open.vanillaforums.com) rather than being separate product lines, so the merged 335-path/380-schema/51-coverable-object union is treated as ONE in-scope surface, not partitioned into in-scope vs out-of-scope families. The SSO/OAuth2/SAML/OIDC/jsConnect authentication FLOWS are deliberately NOT modeled as an 'out-of-scope object family' either -- they have no independently-addressable REST CRUD surface in API v2 at all (they are Dashboard-configured authentication infrastructure, not syncable record types), so they are recorded instead as end-user auth awareness (see EndUserSSOMechanisms) rather than as a scoped-out object family. If a future connector iteration needs SSO CONFIGURATION itself as syncable data, a dedicated follow-up source pass would be needed (no such REST surface was found in this build's evidence trail).
Configuration.PerTenantAddonVarianceNote: Per SOURCE_STUDY.md §8: any given customer Vanilla community may have a DIFFERENT subset of the 51 coverable objects actually enabled depending on which addons that community has turned on (Knowledge Base/Articles, Webhooks, AI settings/processing, third-party integration configs such as Jira/Salesforce/Sprinklr/Hootsuite are all addon-gated). This is normal, expected SaaS-addon variance, not a source-coverage gap -- the Declared metadata seeded from this build's research represents the FULL possible surface across all addons; per-tenant absence of a given addon's objects is handled by runtime discovery / graceful 404 handling at connection time, not by narrowing the Declared catalog itself.
Configuration.ReactionEventScopeNote: CORRECTED (amendment): reaction-EVENT endpoints DO exist and are now emitted as the DiscussionReaction (/discussions/{id}/reactions) and CommentReaction (/comments/{id}/reactions) IOs — each a paginated GET (page/limit) + POST (react) + DELETE .../{userID} (un-react) returning individual reaction events (recordType, recordID, userID, tagID, dateInserted). These are DISTINCT from ReactionType (/reactions), which is the catalog of possible reaction kinds keyed by urlCode. The prior note incorrectly asserted these event endpoints were absent from the merged spec; that was falsifiable against sources/vanilla-openapi.merged.v3.json and is superseded.
